take_homes: Output gets specific when I give the agent specific context: my real numbers, what I hate, a framework I tuned. A better prompt isn't what does it.
Put the rules in a file the agent reads each session, then retro it after the work. The first draft of that file is rarely right.
The agent grades its own work too kindly. Use a cold second reader, and check the claims against what I know.

monday.move: Write a context file for the pricing pilot brief: our sources, which one I distrust (the churn article), and what a good brief looks like. Run the brief on it, then have a cold agent critique the result.
monday.who: Me first, then one teammate from my fourteen to try it
monday.when: Monday morning, before the pricing working group
monday.stop_condition: The cold critic finds no generic claims, or one hour is up
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for context files. Everyone keeps their own copy, so the file stays mine until that's solved.

misconception.why: I came in thinking better prompts were the skill. The module showed the output improving because the context improved while the model stayed the same, so context files matter more than prompt wording. I still caught myself thinking of the rules file as a better prompt.

one_line: The first half repeats one point a few times, but the rules file and the cold critic are worth having, and I'm bringing the pricing pilot to Module 2.
